definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded a mean preference of 0.5135 using a Gaussian trace distribution. This suggests that without specific goal-oriented weighting or high-variance feedback loops, preferences remain close to the initial distribution median, showing minimal path-dependency induced bias.
definition.limitations: The current model uses a simplified trace-weighting mechanism (squared trace values). It does not capture complex reinforcement learning dynamics or multi-stage decision hierarchies.
definition.next_step: Refine the experiment to introduce explicit reward-modulated trace weighting to test if variance increases significantly.

definition.cost: Low; standard Python simulation of trace weighting.
definition.reason: Previous results are inconclusive regarding path-dependency. Modifying the weight mechanism is required to falsify the hypothesis effectively.
definition.stop_condition: If variance fails to correlate with trace-weight modification across three distinct weight-functions.
definition.uncertainty: Unclear whether the lack of variance is due to the simple weight-calculation function or an inherent property of the trace-memory model.
